intent: Support valid learning feedback while separating observed evidence from guesses about proficiency.

rules.title: No proficiency by volume
rules.description: Repeated answers to the same prompt count as practice, not independent transfer, delayed retention or CEFR certification.

rules.title: Meaning over exemplar match
rules.description: An open-ended answer may have valid alternative vocabulary, word order or register; do not mark it wrong merely because it differs from examples.

rules.title: Uncertain stays uncertain
rules.description: If the available evidence cannot establish whether a free response satisfies a rubric, use uncertain and request review or a clearer task.

rules.title: Record help
rules.description: Show and retain which hints, translations and examples were actually used. A demonstrated answer with a visible model is not independent production.

rules.title: Focus feedback
rules.description: Identify what succeeded, prioritize one change with a reason, then invite a meaningful retry. Do not overwhelm beginners with every minor error.

rules.title: Communicative stakes
rules.description: Treat intelligible beginner approximations differently from errors that reverse meaning or make a route/destination unsafe or ambiguous.

rules.title: Separated skills
rules.description: Correct writing does not prove speaking/pronunciation; hearing synthetic TTS is not proof of natural conversational listening.

rules.title: No retrospective mastery
rules.description: Legacy word drills and translations remain valid historical attempts but cannot be silently recategorized as transfer or long-term competence.

rules.title: Non-blocking
rules.description: A learner can continue or retry; missing listening audio, review tooling or storage must never be silently scored as learner failure.

criteria.question: Did the learner achieve the requested communicative purpose?
Is the meaning coherent and compatible with the context?
Are the target-language forms adequate for the learner's stage and do errors hinder interpretation?
Is the tone appropriate to the person and situation?
Was the answer produced without viewing the model or relying on assistance?
Does the answer solve a genuinely different scenario than training?

decisionPolicy: If any essential criterion is notObservable, classify the overall outcome as uncertain.
If communicative intent fails, classify as notSupported with helpful contextual feedback.
Do not conflate orthography errors with failures of meaning when the intent remains clear.
Do not record independentProduction when a modelAnswer was available during response.
Record transfer only when the prompt context differs and the model was unavailable.
Require a reviewed rubric decision for free text; never infer support by literal match alone.

safetyAndPrivacy.externalEvaluation: disabled until user consent, vendor selection, cost and privacy review
